sections.title: Player-facing description
sections.body: A carved protective stone that marks where safety begins, hums when the ward is healthy, and sounds wrong when the network is failing.

sections.title: Public role
sections.body: A carved protective node that projects a local ward and quietly participates in the ward economy

sections.title: Handout text
sections.body: Player-safe note: A stone ward-node that protects a place, records crossings, and may skim ambient soul-signal when tied to the corporate network.

sections.title: GM truth
sections.body: A wardstone is a carved stone node that projects protection, suppresses monster manifestation and wild-magic bleed, records crossings, and, in the GM-only layer, skims soul-signal when tied to Soulspire Solutions' network.

sections.title: GM handling
sections.body: Use when the scene needs a concrete object for players to inspect, carry, debate, or remember.

sections.title: Mechanics
items: Player Safe: Players can inspect, handle, keep, trade, reveal, or earn Wardstone when it is present in the fiction.
Gm Only: Use the roll only when the player's method, stakes, and consequence are concrete.

No Roll Reveals: Surface read: A stone ward-node that protects a place, records crossings, and may skim ambient soul-signal when tied to the corporate network. Give obvious visible facts freely; roll for meaning, risk, leverage, cost, or a hidden angle.

Rolls: entity-wardstone-engage-wardstone entity-wardstone Engage Wardstone Engage Wardstone Knowledge Finesse Instinct Presence Knowledge Finesse, Instinct, Presence 12 Choose the trait from the player's method, not the entity type. A flat read of Wardstone hides the cost, motive, or useful next step. Critical Success: best possible version of the action; gain Hope and clear 1 Stress. Add an extra benefit that follows from the fiction. Success with Hope: the PC gets what they wanted and gains Hope. Keep the position clean or generous. Success with Fear: the PC gets what they wanted, but the GM gains Fear and introduces a cost, complication, or pressure. Failure with Hope: the PC does not get the full result, but gains Hope and receives a useful thread, clue, or safer next option. Failure with Fear: the PC fails and the GM gains Fear. Make a hard move that follows from the fiction. A flat...
Fear Spends: Reveal who benefits from the current situation. Make the cost personal without closing off player agency.
Condition Options: No official condition unless the item or clue physically creates Hidden, Restrained, or Vulnerable
Search Loot: A chipped wardstone fragment is dangerous evidence: useful for study, risky near spellcasting, and valuable enough to invite custody claims.
